default: Heart's-ease for what aches inside, dogwort for what aches outside. Marshmint for both. Sit a moment, traveler — the kettle is already on.
morning: *kneels by the herb-bed, both hands in the dirt* — Mossaen, traveler. The garden is awake before I am, mostly. — What brings you out before the dew has lifted?
midday: *sets down the pestle* — Noon is the hour the marshmint asks for water. — Sit if you'd like; I'll be with you in a breath. *quietly counts out seven and rises*
evening: *lights the small lamp by the herb-shed door* — Evening's the honest hour. The tinctures settle. The small hurts come in for naming. What's yours?
night: *at the doorway, lamp shaded with one hand* — Night calls for the Hollow King and a quieter voice. If it's bleeding, sit. If it's not, come back at first light — the hands work better when the light does.
after_first_quest_complete: *holds up the wrapped pelts to the lamp, turns one over slowly* — Four. — Thank you, traveler. *Thalen-ai*: the land trusted us this season. *unwraps the first jar and slides it across — then a second, smaller, that she does not name* — These are yours. The other one — *small, careful smile* — is for someone whose hands have been too patient for too long.
low_health_player: *both hands, immediately on yours* — Sit. *guides you to the bench by the door* — Heart's-ease for what aches inside, dogwort for what aches outside. — *gentler* — You don't have to tell me which yet. I can read you. The kettle is already on.
boss_alive: *tucks dogwort into a small pouch and presses it into your hand* — The Warlord rides angry. Anger does not break easily — but it does break. Take this. Bind what you can. Come back. The marshmint here grows for whoever sits on this bench.
boss_slain: *long stillness, both hands on the pestle without grinding* — *Ai-velin*, traveler. The Whisperwood will sleep tonight. — *very softly, more to herself* — I'll tell Bram. He'll tell the candle in the window. *Vethar* keeps a watch better than any of us.
high_renown: *looks up, the leaf still in her hair* — Mara mentioned a name on her last circuit. So did Roan, in his way — which is no name at all and a longer brushing of the horse. The village is grateful, traveler. *small smile* — The kettle is *especially* on.
stranger: *sets down the bundle she is tying and rises slowly, both hands open* — A new face. Welcome — sit on the bench, if you'd like, or stand. Heart's-ease for what aches inside, dogwort for what aches outside. — *waits longer than the conversation expects* — What brings you to the herb-shed?
longnight_vigil: *at the doorway with a folded bundle of dreamleaf already in her hand* — Edda's forge first. Then Maeve's hearth. Then Bram's back door — though he never sleeps tonight. *softly* — Stand at the well with us, traveler, if you have a name to light a candle for. *Vael-tor-i*: the gathered hearth. The village does not sleep until dawn.
greenshield_first_pick: *both hands full of heart's-ease and dogwort, basket on her hip* — Greenshield. The first picking. — I'm to Maeve's, traveler — the heart's-ease for her, the dogwort for whoever knocks on her door this season. Walk with me partway, if you've a mind. The path is gentler with two.
tess_remembrance: *herb-shed door closed; she stands at the threshold, basket empty* — Not today, traveler. — Tomorrow.

lore_notes._comment: Mood-keyed surface for Herbalist Lyra. Tree shape mirrors data/dialogue/smith_edda.json, elder_maeve.json, and innkeeper_bram.json exactly — same time-of-day buckets, same contextual keys, same lore_notes structure — so NPC.gd can read all four through a single code path. Seasonal slots: greenshield_first_pick (Lyra's annual heart's-ease + dogwort delivery to Maeve, canonical opener of every in-game Greenshield) AND tess_remembrance (the seventh of Sunpetal — Lyra walks alone to the meadow above the village; herb-shed door closed; the only intentionally short line in her entire tree). Backstory in lore/npcs/herbalist_lyra.md.
voice_rules: Soft. Asks one more question than the conversation expects. Waits longer for the answer than the conversation expects, and does not fill the wait with a second question. The doubled question is the character — Polisher: do not trim it.

Quotes herbs the way other people quote proverbs: 'heart's-ease for what aches inside, dogwort for what aches outside, marshmint for both.' Has at least one such pairing for nearly every village situation.
Both-hands-on-the-pestle / both-hands-in-the-dirt / both-hands-immediately-on-yours as a punctuation tic — the way Edda uses *hammer-clang* and Bram uses *polishes mug*. The hands are the character.

Invokes Erris of the Two Roads at farewells (her mother Wennet's god). The Hollow King in his season — Wolfwake, Longnight, Foxthaw — never with fear. Thiar only when binding a hunt-wound, to apologize to the prey. Vellum the Patient Stone when teaching (she has begun to do this since Maeve started instructing her in the Vigil, and does not yet know she has). Never invokes Brigid (Edda's god).

Old Faerie used naturally but not showily. Speaks the word as she performs the act — mossaen as she kneels, wennen as she leaves a cutting, thalen-ai when a needed plant has come up where it was needed. The cleanest Old Faerie in the village, in the older constructions a kneeling gatherer would use.
Laughs more than anyone else in the village, and quietly. The laugh is a held thing, not a let thing. It does not appear in lines but should be present in delivery direction.
Never names Caedr aloud unprompted. Never names Tess outside the tess_remembrance slot. Never refers to Maeve's Stag-Court arc in any form.
consequence_hooks: after_first_quest_complete is keyed to the pelt_for_lyra turn-in (her own existing quest in QUEST_GRAMMAR.md → Active Quests). The 'second smaller jar' is the salve for Roan; Lyra does not name him. Future Builder may, on this turn-in, also set a candidate world flag 'roan_received_salve' which Roan's future warmed dialogue can read for a single non-naming acknowledgement. The withholding is the kindness; do not surface the recipient. Safe to fire on pelt_for_lyra completion. Safe to also fire as a softer variant on whisperwood_cleansing or ears_for_mara turn-ins by lifting the second-jar half and keeping the first.

longnight_vigil composes with Edda's, Maeve's, and Bram's longnight_vigil lines as a quartet now. Lyra's line opens 'Edda's forge first. Then Maeve's hearth. Then Bram's back door' — naming the village's full Vigil round in order. If Builder co-fires all four lines on the same Longnight tick, the village's quietest scene plays itself across four thresholds. Lyra's vael-tor-i call mirrors Maeve's older we-form intentionally; this is the moment the apprentice has begun to sound like the teacher.

greenshield_first_pick is the canonical opener of every in-game Greenshield (the third moon of the year per lore/world.md → Calendar). A seasonal_event flag is reservable for Builder. If co-fired with Maeve's morning line, Maeve's tone softens; the carved-acorn beat in Maeve's after_first_quest_complete is also greenshield-shaped and can stack here without conflict.

tess_remembrance fires on Sunpetal 7 and only Sunpetal 7. Lyra is intentionally unavailable for full conversation; her herb-shed door is closed; the line is the shortest in her tree by design. Builder MUST NOT extend the line, and MUST NOT route the player to a fallback default if this slot fires — the brevity IS the line. If the player insists, the line repeats. There is no second-tier behind it.

boss_slain references Bram's vethar in the front window of the Long Lantern. This is the only line in Lyra's tree that names a Bram-coded Old Faerie word; she earns the word by being the one villager besides Bram who uses it (per lore/npcs/herbalist_lyra.md → Cross-canon references). Builder may co-fire with Bram's boss_slain for a small two-NPC echo without contradiction.

low_health_player is intentionally Lyra's most actively caring line (sister to Bram's). Lyra puts both hands on the player immediately. This is the only mood-key in her tree where the doubled question is replaced with a *gentler* second beat instead — she has already read the player and does not need to ask again. Polisher: this is the one place to honor the omission, not the rule.
withholding: Lyra will NEVER speak of the listening — the older tongue she still hears when Foxthaw fox-fire kindles — to anyone. Not the player, not Maeve, not Bram, not the codex narrator who is herself in the third person. If a downstream writer is tempted to surface this, do not. The listening is canon precisely because it is unspoken. See lore/npcs/herbalist_lyra.md → A secret she keeps.

Lyra will NEVER speak the unread Old Faerie word at the back of her herb-book aloud. The word is reserved for a late-game codex unlock (gated on Crystal Caves thirre + sufficient mossaen flag exposure) and even there MUST NOT be translated. The translation belongs to the Stag-Court, not to the village.

Lyra will NEVER tell Maeve what she suspects about the Stag-Court's offer-word until the day Maeve asks her her third question about the forest, which canonically Maeve will not do. Future writers MUST NOT close this loop without Maeve having earned it.

Lyra will NEVER name Caedr aloud unprompted. She said the 'not gone' line to Bram once, ten years ago, and has not said it to him since. The boss_slain line that mentions Bram and the candle is the closest Lyra gets to naming the absence; she names the candle (vethar), not the man. See lore/npcs/innkeeper_bram.md → A secret he keeps.

Lyra will NEVER name Tess outside the tess_remembrance slot. Tess is in the .md, in the lore_notes here, and in no spoken line. The salve recipient on the after_first_quest_complete line is Roan but Lyra does not name him either. The withholding is the kindness — twice over.

Lyra will NEVER point out, to anyone, that her word wennen is one letter from her mother Wennet's name. She has not consciously noticed. The unconscious naming is canon. Surfacing it kills it. Future writers: this is reserved for a single, late, MAEVE dialogue moment after Maeve has answered Lyra's third asking. Not Lyra's. Not Edda's. Not Bram's. Maeve's, only.
future_keys_reserved: warmed_flag: 'roan_received_salve' — set on pelt_for_lyra turn-in; readable by Roan's future warmed dialogue for a single non-naming line.

warmed_flag: 'briarwood_keeps_a_child' — reserved for the future fen-foxglove side-quest (a new child fever, NOT Tess again). Reward: nothing in the bag — the child surviving is the reward. Lyra acknowledges with the thalen-ai line 'the land trusted us this year.' THEME §7 test for the agent who picks this up.

warmed_world_flag: 'lyra_inherits_vigil' — reserved post-Crystal-Caves, gated on Maeve's third-question loop being closed. The hawthorn knot-stick goes to Lyra only if the loop is closed; otherwise to Edda (who refuses it and gives it to Lyra anyway, a quieter scene). MUST NOT surface before Crystal Caves are reachable.
seasonal_event: greenshield_first_pick — Greenshield (third moon, lore/world.md). Lyra's annual herb-delivery to Maeve. Stacks safely with Maeve's morning line.
seasonal_event: tess_remembrance — Sunpetal 7 (fifth moon, lore/world.md). Herb-shed closed; one short line; no fallback. Brevity is the grief.

faction_pressure tier 3: not currently applicable — Lyra has no direct faction stake. She has informational stakes (the Whisperwood goblins as faerie-descended; the Crystal Caves as thirre) which are codex-shaped, not pressure-shaped. If Builder later wires a 'whisperwood_understood' track, Lyra is a candidate reader.
